result.sentence: About 210.1 A (174.7 kVA) of this 400 A service is left by the measured-demand method in 2023 NEC 220.87.

work.method: Existing load = maximum demand ÷ power factor × 125%, in amps at the service voltage (single-phase: kVA × 1,000 ÷ V; three-phase: kVA × 1,000 ÷ (√3 × V)); headroom = service rating − existing load.
steps: Data period: the highest 15-minute demand from a recording of at least 30 days: 120.0 kW.
Demand in kVA: 120.0 kW ÷ power factor 0.95 = 126.3 kVA.
Headroom: 400 A − 189.9 A = 210.1 A, or 174.7 kVA.
At power factor 0.90 instead, the headroom is 199.5 A.

Utility meter data is the total for the service and assumes the phases are balanced. The 30-day option is based on the highest-loaded phase, so per-phase recordings, when you have them, replace the meter total.

Method: 2023 NEC 220.87, paraphrased: the existing load is the maximum demand from a year of data, or from 30 days or more of 15-minute recording, taken at 125%. The authority having jurisdiction decides which edition applies and whether this method may be used.
assumptions: The maximum demand is a 15-minute average, the way demand meters and interval files record it.
Utility meter data is the service total and assumes balanced phases.
